Act. Effective July 1, 1070, the state increased all AFCD payments by ten per­cent. However, the increase was short-lived because the much greater than anticipated increase in caseload threatened to greatly overrun the budget, and  by October 1070, it was necessary to rescind the increase and cut back the level of payments to the pre-July 1070 level. In September 1070, an injunction was requested to enjoin the state from continuing to operate in noncompliance with the Social Security Act. The motion for the injunction was opposed on the grounds that only the Legisla­ture could remedy the problem, and that the Legislature would be requested to give top priority to this problem at its next regular session. In an Order entered December 3, 1970, the court allowed the Legislature the requested time to study the problem and to enact new legislation which would put the state back in compliance
